Product Information
Overview

The MagSafe Charger makes wireless charging a snap. The perfectly aligned magnets attach to compatible iPhone models. The MagSafe Charger provides faster wireless charging up to 25W when paired with a 30W power adapter.

The MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W and Qi charging, so it can be used to wirelessly charge your iPhone 8 or later, as well as AirPods models with a wireless charging case.

Available in two cable lengths: 1 meter and 2 meters.

The magnetic alignment experience only applies to iPhone 12, iPhone 13, iPhone 14, iPhone 15, compatible iPhone 16 models, iPhone 17 models, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro models, and iPhone Duo.

Recommended:

For faster wireless charging up to 25W — up to 50 percent battery in around 30 minutes for compatible iPhone 16 models, iPhone 17 models, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro models, and iPhone Duo when paired with the 30W USB‑C Power Adapter (sold separately).**

For fast wireless charging up to 15W for iPhone 12 or later with MagSafe when paired with the 20W USB‑C Power Adapter (sold separately).**

For wireless charging up to 7.5W for iPhone 8 or later with Qi when paired with the 20W USB‑C Power Adapter (sold separately).**

 iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro Models Support 25W Qi2.2 Charging
 Tuesday September 9, 2025 12:46 pm PDT by Juli Clover 
 The iPhone 17 , ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro, and ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max can charge at up to 25W using the next-generation Qi2.2 chargers. Qi2.2 is an upgraded specification that matches the 25W charging speed of the updated MagSafe specification introduced last year. 
Apple debuted ‌MagSafe‌ 2 last year, and the iPhone 16 models, ‌iPhone 17‌, and ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro models can charge at up to 25W over ‌MagSafe‌, so now the new devices will be able to get the same charging speed with Qi2.2.
 Qi2.2 charging speeds require a Qi2.2 charger, and accessory makers are starting to come out with wireless charging options that support the new standard. 
 The iPhone Air is limited to 20W charging over ‌MagSafe‌ and Qi2.2, so it is not able to reach the 25W charging speeds that other models are capable of.

 How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support (BY)

 How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone
 Most iPhone models can charge with MagSafe Charger.
 Set up your MagSafe Charger
 Connect the USB-C connector on your MagSafe Charger to a recommended 30W or greater Apple USB-C power adapter or compatible third-party USB-C adapter. You can also connect to a USB-C port on a Mac or PC.
 Place your MagSafe Charger face up—as shown—on a flat surface, clear of any metal objects or other foreign material.
 Place your iPhone on your MagSafe Charger.
 Get up to 25W faster wireless charging
 The MagSafe Charger is designed to quickly and safely wirelessly charge your iPhone. The system intelligently adapts to conditions to optimize charging your iPhone at up to 25W of peak power delivery for faster wireless charging. The actual power delivered to the iPhone will vary depending on the iPhone model, wattage of the power adapter, and system conditions.
 It's important to plug into a power source before placing your iPhone on the MagSafe Charger. This allows MagSafe to verify it's safe to deliver maximum power. If you happen to place your iPhone on the MagSafe Charger before plugging into a power source, simply remove your iPhone from the MagSafe Charger, wait three seconds, and then put it back on to resume maximum power delivery.
 All power adapters have different ratings for amount and rate of power delivery. The MagSafe Charger requires the following ratings to deliver faster wireless charging.
 Use these power adapters and iPhone models together for up to 25W faster wireless charging
 iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 16 Plus, and iPhone 16 Pro Max
 30W or greater power adapter
 15V/2.0A or higher power adapter
 MagSafe Charger, noted on the device or its cable as part number A3502, A3503, A2580, or A3250
 Higher wattage adapters at or above 15V/2.0A will also deliver a maximum of up to 25W peak power to your iPhone.
 iPhone Air will achieve 20W peak power. iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Pro will achieve 22.5W peak power.
 While you have USB-C or Lightning accessories such as headphones connected to your phone, charging is limited to 16W for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max; 10W for iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max; 7.5W for iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, and iPhone 16 Pro Max; and limited to 16W for iPhone 17 and iPhone Air to comply with regulatory standards.

 Check certification, input requirements, mounting stability, and ventilation. Navigation and hot conditions can affect charging performance. 
 Charging several devices together 
 Check each pad’s output and the adapter’s output allocation when multiple ports or devices are in use. 
 Apple’s current MagSafe Charger is a straightforward reference option because Apple specifies its Qi2 25W certification and 30W-adapter requirement. Third-party products can offer different formats, including stands, power banks, and car chargers, but verify each exact product’s certification and what is included. For example, UGREEN’s U.S. storefront lists MagFlow products advertised at 25W; the listing alone should not be treated as proof of Qi2 25W certification for a particular model.
 What to do if charging seems slower than expected
 Verify the wireless accessory: Confirm its exact model supports Qi2 25W, not only 15W Qi2 or magnetic attachment.
 Check the adapter: Use a 30W-or-higher USB-C adapter that supports USB Power Delivery for the 25W wireless setup.
 Check the connection: Try the charger maker’s supplied or specified cable and make sure the adapter is firmly connected.
 Reposition the phone: Center it on the magnetic charger; remove a thick, metal, or poorly aligned case for a test.
 Reduce heat and workload: Move the setup away from direct heat and pause demanding use while charging.
 Check shared power: Disconnect other devices from a multi-port adapter or stand to see whether its available output changes.
 Compare wired charging: Test with a suitable USB-C cable and adapter. This can help distinguish a wireless accessory issue from a broader phone or power-source issue.
 Check product support: Review the manufacturer’s compatibility notes and firmware guidance for the exact charger.
 Charging power changes during a normal session, so do not judge the accessory from one temporary wattage reading. If the phone or charger is too hot or too cold, fast charging may be unavailable until conditions improve.
